sessions.title: No training logged
sessions.detail: Full rest week — nothing on Strava

strength_detail.focus: First strength touch of the block — two easy rounds, learn the movements, nothing near strain. · 2 easy rounds.

blocks.x: Easy movement — leg swings, hip circles, a flight of stairs.
Slow and controlled; back knee kisses the floor.
Drive through the heel, squeeze at the top.
Balance + hamstrings; reach long, hips square.
Slow 3-second lowering below the step edge.
Short-lever version on a chair or bench is fine — groin insurance.

Low back stays glued to the floor.

Hips quiet — anti-rotation.

sessions.title: Rest / walk
sessions.detail: No bike, no swim this week — three runs, let the legs lead

swim_detail.tag: Kick phase 1 · wake the legs up
swim_detail.focus: First swim of the block. Plain swimming, no buoy — expect the hips to sit a little lower at first; that’s normal and exactly what the kick work is for.

blocks.x: 200 easy — swim it as 4×50 (r15) if the hips sink — + 2×50 as 25 catch-up drill / 25 swim.
Easy-technique pace (1:55–2:05/100). Long relaxed strokes, light steady kick just enough to keep the hips high.

The swim half of each 50 is recovery — the kick dose starts small on purpose. Kick from the hip, not the knee: loose ankles, pointed toes, small fast amplitude — just enough to lift the hips. The point is feel, not effort. Optional short fins to feel the ankle snap.
Very easy, any stroke — let everything go loose.

sessions.title: Strength A1 · squat (evening)
sessions.detail: Squat · RDL · step-up · calves — technique loads · ~35 min

strength_detail.focus: First barbell session. Loads deliberately comfortable — the goal is grooved movement and the DOMS out of the way now, not in October.

blocks.x: Easy spin or brisk walk, hips and ankles loose; then 2 lighter ramp-up sets of the first lift before the work sets.
Technique loads — crisp and comfortable, 3×8–10.
Hinge, soft knees, bar close to the legs; hamstrings load the descent — stop where the back would round.
Onto the jump box or bench; drive through the top leg, control the way down.
Slow 3-second lowering, full stretch at the bottom — long-run insurance at your mileage.
One heavy kettlebell, walk tall, don’t lean — the obliques do the work.
Per side — hips stacked and high.

sessions.detail: Deadlift · split squat · hip thrust — technique loads · ~35 min

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.cue: Technique loads — position over load.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.cue: Rear foot on the bench, KBs or DBs in hand; torso tall, knee tracks the toes.

exercises.name: Hip thrust · bar
exercises.cue: Shoulders on the bench, chin tucked; full lockout with a 1-second squeeze.

exercises.name: Kettlebell swing
exercises.cue: Hardstyle: a hip snap, not an arm lift — power for free at the end of the session.

exercises.name: KB press-out
exercises.cue: Kneeling anti-rotation press-out — the core resists the twist.

exercises.name: Box jump
exercises.cue: Jump up, STEP down — no rebounding. Full recovery between sets; quality over puff.

fuel.intro: Built around your three products. Train your gut with the exact race fuel on the long runs so nothing is new on the day. Easy runs stay water/fasted — save the carbs for quality and distance. Every session in the plan above carries its ⚡ fuel line.
fuel.timing_rule: Start fuelling early (within the first 20–30 min), then every 20–30 min, always with water. Don’t chase the number once your gut complains — back off to Leppin + water and resume gels when it settles.

per_session.session: Swim / easy run ≤8 km / recovery / shakeout

per_session.take: 1 ULTRA gel ~10′ before the main set + 500 ml Leppin
Match race plan exactly — see ladder + race schema
1 Leppin bottle + 1 chew per hour; +1 gel on 3 h rides

ladder.take: 750 ml Leppin + 1 gel + 1 chew (18 km: +1 gel)
1 L Leppin + 3–4 gels + 2 chews — your exact race plan

caution.text: Given your arrhythmia history, caffeine is a possible trigger . Use the caffeine-free flavours by default in training, and only consider a caffeinated gel on race day if your cardiologist/EP is happy with it . Never trial caffeine for the first time on race day.

race_day.intro: Target 5:41/km = 4:00:00 , fuelling ~ 80 g carbs/hr — well within what your IM gut already handles. Everything below must be rehearsed on the Wk 32 race-sim long run (and previewed on the Wk 17 peak long run).
before: 2–3 days out: carb-load ~ 7–8 g/kg/day from familiar carbs; top up between meals with Leppin. Normal sodium, stay hydrated.
Day before: high-carb, low-fat / low-fibre meals; nothing unusual.
3 h before: familiar breakfast ~ 1.5–2 g/kg carbs (e.g. white bread + jam/honey, banana) + 500–600 ml fluid.
15 min before: 1 ULTRA gel (45 g) + a few sips of water.

timeline.take: 1 ULTRA gel (45 g) + sips of water
Start a 500 ml Leppin flask — sip across the hour
1 ULTRA gel (45 g) + start 2nd 500 ml Leppin
1 ULTRA gel (45 g) — caffeine flavour only if EP-cleared
1 chew/gel if the stomach allows — else water
Water / small sips — bring it home

race_day.totals: ~300 g from gels + chews + ~54 g from 2×500 ml Leppin = ~85 g/hr . Want ~80? Drop the 3:30 item. Carry the gels + chews on you; swap/refill the Leppin flask around 2:00; use aid-station water throughout.
race_day.hydration: ~400–500 ml/hr for a cool March race. Leppin carries ~300 mg sodium per 500 ml; add a pinch of salt or an electrolyte tab if it’s warm. Drink to thirst, small and often.
race_day.pacing: First 5 km controlled 5:43–5:45 , settle to 5:39–5:41 , hold. Halfway ~2:00:00. The race is won by not slowing after 32 km — aim 3:58–3:59.

caution.text: Nothing new — only what you rehearsed. Caffeine gels only if EP-cleared. If your gut rebels, drop to water + Leppin and resume gels once it settles. Stop and seek help for chest pain, palpitations, dizziness or fainting.

warmup.intro: You need less warm-up than instinct says . Your opening pace of 5:43–5:45 sits inside your easy band, and the plan’s own “first 5 km controlled” is a 35-minute warm-up. Anything longer spends glycogen you need at 32 km — elites warm up more only because their opening pace is near threshold. This protocol solves logistics, not physiology: staying warm in the corral, loosening ankles and hips, two planned toilet stops, and not going out fast. Rehearse it on the three long runs marked ↻ — nothing new on the day.

timeline.detail: As section 10 — familiar carbs ~1.5–2 g/kg + 500–600 ml.
Bag drop. Toilet #1. Throwaway layer on and staying on. Keep walking — sitting is what stiffens the hips.
Standing circuit below. No static hold longer than 30 s.
5–8 min @6:15–6:30. Only if it is cold or you feel stiff, there is room, and you will be in the corral within 15 min. Otherwise skip it .
Toilet #2. Into the pen. Layer stays on.
1 ULTRA gel (45 g) + sips of water. Caffeine-free unless EP-cleared.
March on the spot 30 s · 15 calf raises · 10 ankle rocks each side · 20 easy knee lifts. Repeat until the gun.
3 × 10–15 s building to marathon pace, no faster . Not strides. Packed corral → skip.
First 5 km at 5:43–5:45 , then settle to 5:39–5:41. Treat km 1–2 as the last of the warm-up and let people go past.

circuit.movement: Ankle rocks — forward/back over the toes
High knees, easy, on the spot
Butt kicks, easy, on the spot

warmup.circuit_note: Nothing on the floor, nothing needing space. No static stretch held past 30 s : holds under 60 s per muscle cost a trivial 1–2% of force, holds over 60 s cost 4–7.5%. Short holds inside a moving warm-up are fine; long ones while you stand waiting are not.

conditions.what: Do the jog. Two throwaway layers, gloves until the gun. Move continuously from −10 — do not stand still.
Skip the jog. Mobility and corral movement only. One throwaway layer. This is the likely March case.
Skip the jog. Mobility down to 4 min. Find shade. Add the pinch of salt from section 10.
The longer the wait, the less worth jogging. Whatever the jog gained is gone by the gun — spend the effort on staying in motion instead.

caution.text: Your HR is capped and blunted , so it cannot tell you when you are warm — go by feel and pace, as everywhere else in this plan. The protocol is deliberately gradual for the same reason. Anything cardiac about race morning is a conversation for your cardiologist/EP, not for this document.
